gap: The number of trees K used for the coniferest bars in Figure 1 is never stated.
chosen: 100 (scikit-learn default), identical for both coniferest and sklearn bars
rationale: The comparison is meant to isolate the implementation, not hyper-parameters; 100 is the IF default in the ecosystem the package mimics.
quote: with K representing the number of trees in the forest

gap: The per-tree training subsample size (max_samples) for the 10^6-sample benchmark is not given.
rationale: Keeps the run comparable to scikit-learn's default IsolationForest and makes fitting negligible relative to scoring, which is the point of the figure.

gap: Random seed / random_state of the tree building for the timing benchmark is not specified.
rationale: Timing of scoring is essentially seed-independent; a fixed seed keeps reruns identical.

gap: What exactly is timed: only the anomaly-score evaluation call, or fit+score; whether warm-up runs are excluded and how many repetitions are averaged.
options: single timed score call, warm-up discarded
chosen: fit once outside the timer, then time the full-dataset score call, discard one warm-up, report the median of >=3 repeats
rationale: The caption says the anomaly score evaluation was measured, and it stresses scoring (not training) as the demanding step.
quote: The dataset anomaly score evaluation has been measured for different versions of scikit-learn.

gap: How single-thread mode is enforced for coniferest (environment variable vs a thread-count argument vs a build without OpenMP).
chosen: OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 plus the library's own thread setting if available
rationale: The figure distinguishes the single-thread bar explicitly, so thread count must be pinned and verified (e.g. by CPU-time/wall-time ratio).

gap: The distribution of the synthetic 10^6 x 2 dataset is not described (uniform vs Gaussian, range, presence of outliers).
chosen: uniform in [0,1]^2 with a fixed seed
rationale: Scoring cost for a tree ensemble depends mainly on N, K and depth, so any bounded 2-D distribution gives the same timing within noise.
quote: A dataset containing ≈106 samples, each having 2 features is considered.

gap: Whether Figure 1 bars are means, medians or single runs, and whether error bars exist (none are drawn).
rationale: No spread is reported, so the grader must compare against a robust central estimate.

gap: Initial value w0 of the AAD regularisation term at the first iteration.

rationale: The paper lists both options and only the previous-iteration choice is meaningful from iteration 2 onward.

gap: Over which set the tau = 0.97 quantile threshold is computed (training sample vs all scored objects, and whether labelled objects are excluded).

rationale: The text defines q_tau as the score limiting the top 1-tau fraction of 'the dataset'.
